title: [Chapitre] VI. Analysis situs (deuxième mouture) : notes manuscrites (18-20/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 66-70 of the 1986 'Analysis situs, deuxième mouture'): Grothendieck is building an axiomatic theory of 'figures' F, a tame or piecewise-linear-like setting. Each figure has a set \tilde F of 'multitubular' sub-figures (cells or strata) X. There is a refinement relation F' << F (subdivision), a restriction F'|X of a refinement of F to a sub-figure X, and an order <= between figures. The question being proved (corollary on p. 68) is a gluing statement. Suppose for every X in \tilde F we are given a refinement F'_X << X, and these are compatible: (F'_Z)|X is defined coherently whenever X <= Z. Then there should be a unique refinement F' of F with F'|X = F'_X for all X, 'the refinement obtained by gluing'.

Page 68 isolates the essential difficulty. One must compare F'_X and F'_Y when X and Y are not comparable. The axiom At W (and the variant At W') says that refinements agreeing on X∩Y (equivalently, on every Z in \hat X ∩ \hat Y) are comparable. This guarantees that the F'_X are mutually compatible, so that Sup_X F'_X can be formed (automatic if \tilde F is finite).

Page 69 finishes the argument:
(1) Set F' = Sup_X F'_X. Then \tilde{F'} = ∪_X \tilde{F'_X}, and F' << F by Axiom 4 (a sup of refinements of sub-figures is a refinement).
(2) To check F'|X = F'_X, he writes F'_X = Sup_{Z ∈ \tilde F} (F'_Z|X). The diagram F'_Z << Z, F' << F, X, X∩Z, together with the margin inequality F'_Z|X <= F'|X << X, shows that the restriction of the sup is the sup of the restrictions. Hence F'|X = F'_X.
(3) Set-theoretically, \tilde{F'} → \tilde F is the gluing of the pieces \tilde{F'_X} → \tilde X over the admissible covering family {\tilde X} of \tilde F. In other words, refinements form a sheaf on the poset or site of cells.

Corollary 2 then generalizes. Under the hypotheses of Cor. 3 on p. 66 (F covered by sub-figures F_i), a compatible family of refinements F'_i of the F_i ('definition to be found') is induced by a refinement F' of F (continued on p. 70). For finite I this already follows from a weaker axiom. Cor. 3 on p. 70 specializes to disjoint sums: Raff(F ⊔ G) ≅ Raff(F) × Raff(G).

Purpose: to establish within the axiomatics that 'subdivisions are local'. This is the descent or sheaf property of the functor Raff on a figure's cells, needed for a tame-topology foundation in the spirit of Esquisse §5.
errors: The argument is sketchy. The identity F'_X = Sup_Z (F'_Z|X) and the commutation of restriction with Sup are asserted via a diagram, not proved from stated axioms. A long deleted passage shows Grothendieck himself was unsure which condition justified it.
Existence of Sup F'_X for infinite \tilde F is assumed, not derived; he notes it is automatic only for finite \tilde F.
In Corollary 2 the notion of 'compatible' family of refinements is explicitly left undefined ('définition à trouver'). The statement is therefore not yet precise.

ideas.what: Gluing of compatible local refinements (subdivisions) on cells into a unique global refinement: a sheaf property of Raff over the poset of multitubular sub-figures.
ideas.modern_name: Locality of subdivisions; refinements of cell or stratified complexes form a sheaf / satisfy descent
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore of PL topology (Whitehead, Zeeman, Rourke–Sanderson; cell-complex subdivision theory)
ideas.where_published: Only the general tame-topology programme is sketched in Esquisse d'un programme §5; this axiomatic development is unpublished.

ideas.what: Axiom At W / At W': refinements of non-comparable cells X, Y that agree on X∩Y are comparable. Identified as exactly what is needed for compatibility in gluing.
ideas.modern_name: Amalgamation / pushout condition for subdivisions over intersections
ideas.usually_credited_to: No specific attribution; analogous to amalgamation conditions in cell-complex and o-minimal cell decomposition theory

ideas.what: Raff(F ⊔ G) ≅ Raff(F) × Raff(G) for disjoint sums (next page), and its generalization to disjoint families.
ideas.modern_name: Product decomposition of subdivisions over disjoint unions

missed.claim: The axiomatic framework (figures, multitubular sub-figures, refinements, axioms At W/W', Ax 4) with an explicit sheaf/gluing theorem for refinements was left unfinished. Notably the definition of a compatible family of refinements over a covering is 'to be found'. This is part of the unpublished axiomatization of 'topologie modérée' foreshadowed in Esquisse §5.
missed.quote: si on se donne une (F'_i des raffinements des F_i) compatibles (définition à trouver), alors il existe un raffinement F' de F
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is a concrete data point on how Grothendieck intended tame topology to be axiomatized: via a sheaf of subdivisions on a poset of cells rather than via definable sets. This could be compared with o-minimal cell decomposition and with combinatorial models such as exit-path categories. The content itself is elementary.

deep.surprise_reason: The page completes a routine gluing argument (subdivisions defined cellwise glue), standard in PL topology. Its interest is only as an unpublished piece of Grothendieck's tame-topology axiomatics, with the amalgamation axiom At W isolated as the key condition.
transcription_corrections: 'par Ax 4': the image reads 'At 4' or 'Ax 4' (axiom 4), consistent with the axiom labels At W elsewhere.
Deleted bracketed passage: likely 'vu la condition des raffinements F'_Z de F sur les sous-multitubulaires X de F' (not 'sous-triangles'), followed by 'les syst. des F'_Z ...'.
'des sympt. des \tilde{F'_x}' is better read 'des syst.[èmes] des \tilde{F'_x}'.
Corollaire 2 parenthesis: reads '(F'_i des raffinements des F_i) compatibles (définition à trouver)'; the struck word is probably 'syst.'.
Margin: 'Sup_Z F'_Z = F' << F', with '≥' below, then 'F'_Z|X ≤ F'|X << X'.
'ce qui est automatique si on suppose \tilde F fini' is confirmed.
